newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: RALLYING-ERIKSSON AMD MAKINEN DUEL FOR SUPREMACY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-ERIKSSON AMD MAKINEN DUEL FOR SUPREMACY.

text.p: Swede Kenneth Eriksson held a 14 seconds lead over world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland after a thrilling duel in the Portuguese Rally on Monday.
Once championship leaders Colin McRae and Carlos Sainz retired with mechanical problems, the two Scandinavians took turns at the front during 170 km of stages held on gravelled roads.
Eriksson, who won the Swedish Rally last month, went ahead on the sixth stage from Subaru team mate McRae when the British driver was forced out with engine problems.

Makinen, in a Mitsubishi, slowly chipped away at the lead and moved in front at the end of the ninth stage. But he dropped to second again on the 11th when Eriksson opted for a wider-treaded tyre which paid dividends on the loose surface.
"It obviously proved a bit of a winner," said a Subaru team spokesman. "The conditions were very dusty and being first on the road definitely helped as well. Kenneth is feeling really confident now."
Eriksson is currently fourth in the championship and a victory in Portugal, the fourth event in this year's calendar, would give him the lead.
Although McRae was able to push the car to the end of the stage, he did not reach the service point in time and was forced out.

"It is more than a disappointment," he said. "Everything felt good on this event and we were pulling out a good lead. It is easy to say now, but I had a feeling about this one and believe we could have won it."
Sainz had also been in contention during the opening stages when he encountered gearbox problems on the fifth stage.

"Everything was going fine in the stage and it would have been a good time, but just two kilometres from the end there was a big bang in the transmission," said the Spaniard, currently second in the championship behind McRae.
"Maybe something in the gearbox tried to seize, but there was nothing we could do and I was forced to park the car."

Belgian Friday Loix ended the day in third place, more than a minute adrift of the leaders in his Toyota, with Briton Richard Burns fourth and Portugal's Rui Madeira fifth. The rally ends on Wednesday.
